source: Second reference video, transcribed and timed the same way; 170s vertical explainer.
note: Held out on purpose. The contract was derived from the cobra video alone, so this fixture is the generalization test: it is the same storytelling mode with a different close.

observed.hook_type: Opens with a provocative 'why did [powerful group] do [terrible thing]' framing, promising an 'explained like you're five' simplification, paired with a bold national symbol filling the frame.
observed.story_pattern: Numbered chronological steps ('Step one, Step two...') advancing through dates and escalating consequences, building a cause-and-effect chain that culminates in a moral summation and a repeated pattern statement.
observed.recurring_characters: Simple round-headed stick figures split into two visually coded classes: an oppressed population in plain robes versus a powerful class marked by hats/crowns/uniforms, with occasional single named authority figures.
observed.location_reuse: A rotating set of stock settings — outdoor landscape with symbol, industrial cityscape, ornate interiors, barren drought fields, docks/ships, formal meeting rooms — each reused to match the narration beat.
observed.visual_composition: Hand-drawn cartoon illustrations, vertical full-frame, single scene per block; some frames use split-screen contrast or stacked before/after panels to juxtapose two conditions.
observed.on_screen_text: A short 1-3 word caption sits centered low on each frame, echoing a key phrase from the narration at that moment rather than full subtitles.
observed.narrator_tone: Cold, clipped, morally damning documentary voice; short declarative sentences, heavy repetition of a phrase to hammer the pattern, escalating from explanatory to accusatory.
observed.humour_and_interrupts: Dark ironic beats delivered deadpan (e.g. 'the response is immediate and precise. They do almost nothing') and grim juxtapositions used as bitter punchlines rather than jokes.
observed.reveal_placement: The emotional gut-punch statistic and the 'it was never natural, it was policy' reveal land in the final third, right before the wrap-up.
observed.ending_callback: Closes by folding the whole story into a single line, then pivots abruptly to a sponsor pitch for an app, framing consuming such content as self-improvement with a direct call to download.

story.title: Why the British Starved the Indians
story.start_state: India is the richest colony on earth and its farmers grow the food

hook.line: Why the British starved the Indians.

steps.label: 1858, direct rule
steps.situation: Britain takes direct control of India and extracts its wealth on a scale without precedent.

steps.label: The most profitable colony in history
steps.situation: The arrangement is enormously profitable and is treated as a working system.

steps.label: A tax system built to transfer wealth upward
steps.situation: A tax system is designed to move wealth upward to British landlords, administrators and shareholders.

steps.label: Taxed past the ability to eat
steps.situation: The people growing the food are taxed so heavily they cannot afford to eat it.

steps.label: Until the rains stop
steps.situation: The system works perfectly until the rains stop.

steps.label: They do almost nothing
steps.situation: The monsoon fails, people begin to starve, and the colonial response is to do almost nothing.

steps.label: Food leaves anyway
steps.situation: Grain sits in warehouses and is exported to Britain because the market says it is more profitable there.

steps.label: Relief is punished
steps.situation: An official who sets up famine relief is removed for generosity, rations are cut, and anyone able to walk to a camp is turned away as too healthy to need it.

steps.label: Bengal, 1943
steps.situation: Food shipments are diverted away from a fourth famine in Bengal and three million more people die.

steps.label: Then it simply stops
steps.situation: After independence India never has a famine again, which shows the famines were caused by policy and not by drought.

steps.label: The verdict
steps.situation: Twenty-nine million people in the richest colony the world had seen were starved to death by the extraction system and the people running it.
